minutes.headline: Water commissioners backed an SRF application for the Hickory Hills PFAS plant and authorized the audit letter.
minutes.summary: The commissioners reviewed the state revolving fund application for a Hickory Hills PFAS treatment plant, whose figures were described as deliberately inflated placeholders. They authorized the annual audit engagement, agreed to move banking to Enterprise with a new 11-month CD, and discussed the wetlands appeal site visit, the Mass Ave water main bid, a health insurance buyback and a Zone 2 bylaw change.

public_comment.topic: A resident asked about the DEP site visit and appeal, the PFAS plant cost, the bank fees and CD term, the Woodlands lease and right-of-way, and Howard Street. Board and staff answered at length.

votes.motion: Authorize the chair to sign the annual audit engagement letter

budget_items.topic: SRF funding application, Hickory Hills treatment plant
budget_items.what_was_said: The application carries intentionally inflated preliminary budget numbers just to get on the list. Nothing binds the district financially at this point.
The auditor's fee rose again, and it was discussed whether to seek other quotes next year. The board agreed to proceed this year.
Enterprise matched the competing 11-month CD rate and keeps the other rates and fee waivers. Rollstone offered lower rates and some fees.
Another district pays a stipend to employees who opt out. Comparable towns' amounts were compared.

budget_items.topic: ARPA funding request via Select Board
budget_items.what_was_said: The district asked the town for ARPA money for pilot studies, public education and a PFAS master plan.
Collections are improving through payment plans and a fuel assistance program for water bills.

decisions.decision: Put a million and a half into an 11-month CD at Enterprise, close Rollstone, and consolidate the idle money market accounts; no vote taken.
Support taking the Zone 2 bylaw change to town meeting, limited to the Zone 2 changes and the added area.
Hickory Hills pilot study scheduling stays on hold until the appeal is finalized.
Keep the 23rd meeting; the bid opening on the 31st is open to commissioners, and a special meeting can be posted afterward.
Board in concept for a health insurance buyback with proof of coverage and proration; the superintendent will draft the form and finalize at the next meeting.

what_happened.line: Commissioners agreed to move banking to Enterprise, with a new 11-month CD and the Rollstone account closed; no vote was taken.
A motion to authorize the chair to sign the annual audit engagement letter was made; the minutes record the result as not audible.
The board reviewed the state revolving fund application for a Hickory Hills PFAS plant, described as carrying intentionally inflated placeholder figures that bind nothing.
The board supported taking a Zone 2 bylaw change to town meeting, and agreed in concept to a health insurance buyback to be drafted for the next meeting.
Hickory Hills pilot study scheduling stays on hold until the wetlands appeal is finalized.

why_it_matters: The PFAS plant application only secures a place on the state funding list, so the figures in it are not a cost estimate and nothing is yet committed against water rates.
A Zone 2 bylaw change headed to town meeting is a vote residents will be asked to take, and the health insurance buyback would be a new recurring benefit cost once adopted.
